request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows a "Watched due total" for the signed-in user: the due-totals of the people they watch, added up, or 0.00 if they watch no one. All 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

It was a front-end-only change. The app already stores who each user watches and sends it with each person, so I didn't need to change the database or the server.

- **`src/main/frontend/src/app/core/figures.ts`**: a new `watchedDueTotal` adds up the due-total of each watched person. It uses the same per-person figure as the people list, so the two always agree. A person whose due-total shows as "n/a" (no rate for their grade) adds nothing.
- **`src/main/frontend/src/app/features/header/header.ts`**: the new value is shown with `data-testid="watched-due-total"`, next to the other "My …" figures. I also updated the comment that describes what the header shows.
